outcome: Give farm operations director / food quality head a governed method to improve rejected export consignments using phytosanitary certificates, shipment lots and customs rules, with final decisions…
overview: Agricultural Trade and Export Documentation addresses source evidence is scattered across documents and transaction systems, leading to repeated checks and incomplete case files in agriculture and food production operations. The first proof of value uses phytosanitary certificates, shipment lots and customs rules. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is rejected export consignments, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: phytosanitary certificates, shipment lots and customs rules; define rejected export consignments and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Farm Operations Director / Food Quality Head.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including run golden documents and exceptions against the system of record.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
